1.sofaString: 114	Pt, *******, is a 7 month old female who is diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy who is being referred by ***** ****** **** for heart transplant Psychosocial Assessment.  Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the pt's parents and review of the medical records.   SW spent 75 minutes of face to face time with patient and family.     Living situation:  **, *******, lives with her parents and sister in ******, *******.  They reside in a 4 bedroom, 3.5 bathroom home with city water and central heating and a/c.  They have a big air filter that is changed every 6 months as per recommended guidelines.  They use bottled water for drinking.  There is no smoking in the home.  They have no pets.       Demographics:  Mother: ******** *******  DOB:  **/**/****           Age:  34  Education:  ***  Employment:  Not currently employed  Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Father: ****** ******  DOB:  **/**/****     Age:  39  Employment:  ******* Hospital Internal Medicine MD.  Works 10 days on/ 4 days off  Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Siblings:  Sister: ****** ******   Age:  3   No medical problems      Currently has a nanny at bedside as well. She is from ***** and is Spanish-speaking only.  She will be assisting with caring for ****** for the next month.     Support systems:  The family is originally from ********.  Dad's extended family resides in ********.  Mom's mother resides in *****.  They have no family members locally.  However, they are resourceful.  They currently have a nanny who is a friend of the family who came from ***** ** assist.  When she leaves, they are hopeful that a cousin from ******** will be able to come to help.      Dad reports that he came to the US for residency after attending ****** ** ********. He met mom in college in ********, where she was studying for her ***.  They married and she accompanied him to the US.  They describe that they gain support from one another. They also state their religious belief is a source of strength and support. They identify as Catholic.       They had enrolled ****** in a Catholic preschool prior to ******* being ill. They are researching Catholic ********** locally so they can continue her learning exposure.  They are looking for one that has a Spanish speaking teacher, as she is more comfortable with that. However, they would prefer that she speak ******* only at home, and use English at school.  They are touring **** ******* on Wednesday afternoon.     Both parents have a car. They deny that transportation will be a problem.  Mom plans to keep a car with her for travel between local apartment and the daycare and hospital. Her current plan is to have nanny stay at bedside at night so she can care for ******. She will then drop ****** off at school, and will take nanny to apartment so she can rest.  Mom will stay at bedside with ******* during the day.       They also plan to have nanny and ****** return home for 3 days every other week, so that ****** can be in her own bed and have time away from the hospital. During those 3 days, dad's work schedule allows him to be home by noon, which will allow him to have time with ****** as well.     The family has already rented an apartment locally for a one month *****.  At the end of this *****, they plan to move into a transplant housing condo.       Course of illness:     ******* is a 7 mo old female with no past medical history.  Parents had observed fussiness, fatigue with feeds, and difficulty rolling over and sitting up. In addition, she had begun to reflux with feeds and was not responding to prevacid.  She had an appt with GI to evaluate feeding intolerance. At this appt, ******* exhibited significant retractions and tiredness.  GI referred to cardiology.  An echo was performed which revealed a severely dilated RV and LV with decreased cardiac function and EF 20-30%.  She was then referred for admission to *****.  She underwent a cardiac cath which revealed coarctation of the aorta. She underwent ************ on **/**.  She was managed on milrinone and dopamine.  She was then transferred to ** ****** ****** for transplant evaluation.         Financial Situation:     ******* is covered by UHC insurance through dad's employer.  Dad states this is a *** account and has a maximum deductible per ******** year of $5000.  The family is financially supported by dad's income.  The family is doing well financially.  However, dad disclosed that it will be challenging to pay for their home mortgage and the local apartment. He states they can still make ends meet but it will be tight. He is interested in fundraising. Information on fundraising through **** was provided.        Family History:     There is no family medical history of cardiac problems or any other medical problems.  Grandparents on both sides are still living.  There is no reported family history of mental health issues.  There is no reported history of substance abuse.  There is no reported history with law enforcement or DCF.       Adherence:  There are no concerns for adherence identified.  Dad is a MD and states he is quite comfortable with caring for *******.  Mom also states she does not foresee any difficulties administering meds or providing care for *******.  ******* was only on prevacid in the past.  However, mom states she will be able to give multiple meds on a prescribed schedule with no difficulty.  She states they will do whatever it takes to keep ******* healthy.  She states her fear is that ******* will need a 2nd transplant.  She wants to do everything they can on their end to decrease the risk of this.         Assessment and recommendations:     Both parents verbalize that it is hard to know that ******* may need a new heart, as she seemed to be a normal healthy baby initially.  Mom states it is hard for her to see ******* going through all of this, and to know another child has to die in order for her to get a heart.  However, mom states she is hoping for the best for *******.  Dad states it is hard for him because he understands the medical side of things 'too well'.  He states it is hard when it is your own child.  However, both parents express wanting to move forward with transplant.           IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  1     Family Background & Social Support -  2     Financial/Insurance  - 1     Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 1     Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  1     Adherence - 1     Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  1     Health Literacy -  1     Coping Skills - 1     Total:  10 Low Risk     The family scores as low risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.       Recommendations are listed below:     Recommendations:  *Provide ongoing education to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.    *Provide fundraising resources to assist the family with expenses that arise secondary to child's extended admission            ****** ******** LCSW  Pediatric Heart/ Lung Transplant Team  ***-***-****
